1.s: God’s power has given us everything for life and godliness. Add to faith goodness, knowledge, self-control, perseverance, godliness, kindness and love. Peter recalls the transfiguration; prophecy came from people “moved by the Holy Spirit”.
1.d: Peter saw Christ’s glory with his own eyes, and Scripture is completely reliable [[tosn:2 Peter 1:16-21]]: “holy men of God spoke, being moved by the Holy Spirit” [[bible:2 Peter 1:21]]. The prophets did not have to interpret God’s visions alone; God made the meaning clear to them [[tosn:2 Peter 1:20-21]].

2.s: False teachers will arise, as false prophets did, and judgement will come on them as on the angels, the flood and Sodom.
2.d: Chapter 2 often runs close to Jude: compare 2:4 with Jude 6 and 2:13 with Jude 12 [[tosn:2 Peter 2:4]] [[tosn:2 Peter 2:13]].

3.s: Scoffers ask where Christ’s coming is. “One day is with the Lord as a thousand years.” God is patient, “not wishing that anyone should perish, but that all should come to repentance.” New heavens and a new earth are coming.
3.d: Peter speaks of Paul’s letters alongside “the other Scriptures” [[bible:2 Peter 3:16]], suggesting he saw them as carrying God’s authority [[tosn:2 Peter 3:16]]. God is not slow to keep his promise; he is patient [[bsn:2 Peter 3:1-10]].
